Simulate a linear model

Source: R/simulation.R
ctrl_simulate.Rd

Compute the state and output trajectories of a linear time-invariant model driven by an input signal.

Usage

ctrl_simulate(
  sys,
  input = NULL,
  times = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  hold = c("zoh", "foh")
)

Arguments

sys

A model (transfer functions are realized with ctrl_tf2ss()).

input

Input signal (see details).

times

Strictly increasing time points. For discrete models the default is 0:steps * dt with steps = nrow(input) - 1.

x0

Initial state (default zero).

hold

"zoh" or "foh" input interpretation for continuous models.

Value

A ctrl_response object with time, and arrays x (time x states x 1), y (time x outputs x 1) and u (time x inputs x 1), plus the signal names. Use as.data.frame() for a long data frame and plot() for a plot.

Details

Input format. input is either NULL (zero input), a numeric matrix with one row per time point and one column per input (a vector is accepted for single-input models), or a function function(t) returning the input vector at time t (it is evaluated on the time grid).

Continuous time. The simulation is exact for the chosen input interpretation. With hold = "zoh" the input is held at u(t_k) on \([t_k, t_{k+1})\); with hold = "foh" it is linearly interpolated between u(t_k) and u(t_{k+1}). Each step uses the matrix exponential of the corresponding block matrix (see ctrl_c2d()), so there is no integration error. The grid may be irregular; transition matrices are cached for repeated step sizes.

Discrete time. The recurrence \(x_{k+1} = A x_k + B u_k\) is evaluated exactly. times must be the sample instants \(t_0 + k\,dt\); hold is ignored.

Outputs follow \(y_k = C x_k + D u_k\) at every time point.

See also

ctrl_step(), ctrl_impulse(), ctrl_initial()

Examples

sys <- ctrl_ss(-1, 1, 1)
times <- seq(0, 5, by = 0.05)
r <- ctrl_simulate(sys, input = sin(times), times = times)
head(as.data.frame(r))
#>   time       case   kind signal       value
#> 1 0.00 simulation output     y1 0.000000000
#> 2 0.05 simulation output     y1 0.000000000
#> 3 0.10 simulation output     y1 0.002437513
#> 4 0.15 simulation output     y1 0.007187567
#> 5 0.20 simulation output     y1 0.014125209
#> 6 0.25 simulation output     y1 0.023125532
# Free response of x' = -x from x(0) = 1 equals exp(-t)
free <- ctrl_simulate(sys, times = times, x0 = 1)
max(abs(free$x[, 1, 1] - exp(-times)))
#> [1] 9.992007e-16
